title: Blog - SQLi Login Bypass (Easy)
description: Bypass authentication on the blog login form without knowing the administrator password using basic SQL injection.
hints: Check how username and password inputs are concatenated into the SQL statement.
SQL comment syntax '--' or '/*' can comment out the rest of the query.

title: Blog - SQLi Login Bypass (Medium)
description: Bypass the blog login when standard SQL injection keywords or space characters are partially filtered or blacklisted.
hints: Inspect the filter rules: is the application stripping keywords case-sensitively or using simple regex?
Consider using inline comments `/**/` or alternative whitespace characters if standard spaces are blocked.

title: Blog - SQLi Login Bypass (Hard)
description: Bypass a hardened authentication barrier employing parameter sanitization, multi-word blocklists, and quote escaping.
hints: Look for secondary entry points or parameter pollution that alters query execution without triggering the blacklist.
Evaluate alternate encodings or non-standard SQL boolean expressions that remain valid SQLite syntax.

title: Blog - UNION Data Extraction (Easy)
description: Extract secret flag data from the blog database using a classic UNION-based SQL injection attack on the post search parameter.
hints: Determine the number of columns returned by the original query using 'ORDER BY n' or 'UNION SELECT NULL, ...'.
Locate which reflected column displays on screen, then query the flag table or configuration table.

title: Blog - UNION Data Extraction (Medium)
description: Perform UNION extraction when common keywords like 'UNION' or 'SELECT' are stripped by a single-pass filter.
hints: If the application removes 'UNION' once, try nested keywords like 'UNIUNIONON'.
Check if mixed capitalization such as 'uNiOn sElEcT' bypasses a case-sensitive regex.

title: Blog - UNION Data Extraction (Hard)
description: Extract sensitive flag data when UNION queries are blocked or output is blind, requiring boolean-based or error-based extraction.
hints: Test conditional responses using SUBSTR(), INSTR(), or conditional CASE statements.
Automate character-by-character extraction to reconstruct the flag from blind boolean differentials.

title: Blog - Stored XSS in Comments (Easy)
description: Inject an unescaped script tag into the public comment section that executes in visitor and administrator sessions.
hints: Submit basic HTML tags like `<script>alert(1)</script>` into the comment author or body fields.
Review the rendered DOM to see if the comment content is rendered raw without HTML entity encoding.

title: Blog - Stored XSS in Comments (Medium)
description: Bypass a naive comment filter that strips `<script>` tags to execute JavaScript and extract the secret token.
hints: HTML event handlers like `` or `
Inspect whether attributes or nested tags allow JavaScript execution.

title: Blog - Stored XSS in Comments (Hard)
description: Execute JavaScript stored in comments despite character blacklists, CSP restrictions, or attribute sanitization.
hints: Examine Content-Security-Policy headers or HTML sanitizers for gadget libraries or unsafe-inline directives.
Use alternative payload encodings or autofocus/onfocus vectors to trigger script execution.

title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Easy)
description: Access private notes belonging to other users by manipulating sequential numerical identifiers in the API request.
hints: Inspect the URL parameter when viewing a note (e.g., /api/notes/42 or ?id=1).
Increment or decrement the note ID to discover private notes belonging to the administrator.

title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Medium)
description: Access restricted notes protected by client-side checks or disguised identifier formats.
hints: Check if note IDs are encoded (e.g., Base64, hex, or predictable hashes) rather than random UUIDs.
Ensure you send direct API requests rather than relying on UI link restrictions.

title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Hard)
description: Retrieve unauthorized confidential notes through second-order IDOR or mass-assignment in search and export endpoints.
hints: Investigate bulk export, note duplication, or search filter parameters for unauthenticated access.
Check if passing array parameters or JSON object manipulation exposes notes across tenant boundaries.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Easy)
description: Elevate your regular user account to administrator via an unprotected role parameter during profile update.
hints: Inspect the JSON payload sent when updating your user profile.
Add `"role": "admin"` or `"is_admin": true` to the profile update request.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Medium)
description: Bypass role protection on user management endpoints using parameter pollution or header overrides.
hints: Check if administrative routes accept alternate HTTP methods (PUT vs POST vs PATCH).
Inspect custom headers such as `X-User-Role` or `X-Original-URL` that backend proxies might respect.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Hard)
description: Achieve administrative privileges by chaining prototype pollution or session tampering in note-sharing logic.
hints: Analyze how shared note permissions merge user objects in Node.js.
Look for JSON prototype pollution (`__proto__` / `constructor`) affecting authorization checks.

title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Easy)
description: Download unauthorized system files by traversing directories in the file download parameter.
hints: Test relative path sequences like `../../../../flag.txt` or `../../../../etc/passwd` in the filename parameter.
Analyze the error message if the file is not found to understand the storage root directory.

title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Medium)
description: Bypass simple path traversal sanitizers that strip single `../` strings or require specific file extensions.
hints: Try nested traversal sequences such as `....//` or `..././` that reconstitute `../` after single-pass removal.
Test URL encoding (`%2e%2e%2f`) or double encoding (`%252e%252e%252f`).

title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Hard)
description: Circumvent strict canonical path validation or prefix constraints to retrieve secret files.
hints: Check if the application verifies that the path starts with an allowed directory (e.g., `/uploads/`), and append traversal after it.
Explore null-byte termination or absolute path handling on Python `os.path.join` nuances.

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Easy)
description: Upload executable files directly to the server without file type or extension validation.
hints: Upload files with executable extensions or HTML/SVG files that can execute in context.
Check where uploaded files are stored and whether they are directly accessible.

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Medium)
description: Bypass blacklisted extensions on file upload using alternative extensions or case variations.
hints: If `.py` or `.html` is blocked, try `.pht`, `.htm`, or uppercase variants like `.Py`.
Check if the extension check splits only on the first or last period.

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Hard)
description: Achieve remote code execution or arbitrary file write via file upload with content inspection and extension filters.
hints: Test polyglot files that satisfy image header validation (magic bytes) while embedding executable code.
Look into filename path traversal during upload to overwrite application templates or configuration.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Easy)
description: Bypass client-side MIME checks by tampering with the Content-Type header in the upload request.
hints: Inspect the HTTP multipart request when uploading a file.
Modify the `Content-Type: text/plain` header to `image/png` or `image/jpeg` to satisfy server validation.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Medium)
description: Bypass server MIME sniffing by prepending valid file signatures (magic bytes) to unauthorized files.
hints: Add magic bytes for a GIF (`GIF89a;`) or PNG (`\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n`) at the start of your payload.
Verify that the MIME detector reads only the first few bytes while the parser executes the full content.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Hard)
description: Exploit image processing parser quirks or SVG XML entities to bypass comprehensive MIME validation.
hints: Test SVG images with embedded XML External Entity (XXE) or script directives.
Examine how PIL/Pillow or file-type libraries handle multi-stream or corrupted image containers.

title: Shop - Weak JWT None Algorithm (Easy)
description: Forge an administrative authentication token by exploiting the JWT 'none' algorithm flaw.
hints: Decode the JWT header and payload (base64url).
Change the header algorithm `"alg": "HS256"` to `"none"` (or `"None"`), modify user claims, and remove the signature.

title: Shop - Weak JWT Secret Brute Force (Medium)
description: Crack a weak, dictionary-based HMAC secret key used to sign session JWTs and forge an admin token.
hints: Extract the session JWT from cookies or headers and use a tool or script to test common passwords.
Once cracked, sign a modified JWT with `"role": "admin"` using the discovered secret.

title: Shop - Weak JWT Header Parameter Confusion (Hard)
description: Exploit JWT header injection (e.g., `jwk`, `jku`, or `kid` path traversal) to verify forged tokens.
hints: Inspect if the JWT verification checks the `kid` (Key ID) header parameter against a local file.
Point `kid` to an empty file or known static file (`/dev/null`), signing with an empty secret.

title: Shop - No Login Rate Limiting (Easy)
description: Brute-force user credentials on the login endpoint due to absent rate limiting or lockout protections.
hints: Observe that the login endpoint does not enforce delays or account lockouts upon consecutive failures.
Run a credential stuffing script with a common wordlist against the admin account.

title: Shop - Header-Bypass Rate Limiting (Medium)
description: Bypass IP-based rate limiting on login attempts by spoofing client IP header values.
hints: Inspect proxy headers like `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, or `Client-IP`.
Rotate the spoofed IP address in each request to reset the rate limiting bucket.

title: Shop - Timing/Response Attack (Hard)
description: Enumerate valid usernames and exploit subtle response differences or timing attacks to compromise credentials.
hints: Measure response times or status code nuances between valid and invalid usernames.
Leverage password reset or registration error messages to confirm target accounts before targeted attacks.

title: Shop - Predictable Reset Token MD5 (Easy)
description: Predict password reset tokens generated from weak cryptographic primitives such as unsalted MD5 of username.
hints: Request a password reset for your own test account and examine the reset token structure.
Check if the token matches `md5(username)` or `md5(email)`.

title: Shop - Predictable Reset Timestamp (Medium)
description: Crack password reset tokens derived from predictable server epoch timestamps.
hints: Analyze token entropy; does it vary strictly according to the Unix epoch second of the request?
Record server response headers (`Date`) and brute-force the narrow timestamp window.

title: Shop - Host Header Poisoning Reset (Hard)
description: Poison password reset links by manipulating the HTTP Host or X-Forwarded-Host header to intercept tokens.
hints: Provide a custom `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Host` header when requesting a password reset for the admin.
Verify whether the reset link sent to the user contains your controlled attacker domain.

title: PingTool - Unsanitized Command Injection (Easy)
description: Execute arbitrary OS commands on the ping utility via unescaped shell concatenation.
hints: Append shell command separators such as `;`, `&&`, or `|` after the target IP.
Execute commands like `; cat /flag.txt` or `; id` to read the challenge flag.

title: PingTool - Filter-Bypass Command Injection (Medium)
description: Bypass a command injection filter that blacklists standard shell metacharacters like `;` and `&`.
hints: Test newline characters (`%0a` or `\n`) or command substitution syntax like `$(...)` or backticks `` `...` ``.
Check if pipeline `|` or redirection `<` can execute commands without semicolons.

title: PingTool - Whitespace/Binary Bypass Command Injection (Hard)
description: Execute shell commands under strict filters forbidding spaces, slashes, and common executable names.
hints: Use shell environment variables like `${IFS}` to substitute for whitespace.
Use wildcard expansion (`/???/c??` for `/bin/cat`) or base64 decoding to bypass keyword filters.

title: PingTool - Unrestricted SSRF (Easy)
description: Reach internal network endpoints and services through the unvalidated HTTP health check feature.
hints: Submit loopback or internal addresses like `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` or `http://localhost:5000/`.
Explore internal admin endpoints or cloud metadata services reachable from the container.

title: PingTool - SSRF Localhost Filter Bypass (Medium)
description: Bypass basic regex filters blocking the literal strings 'localhost' and '127.0.0.1'.
hints: Use alternative IP notations for 127.0.0.1 such as decimal (`2130706433`), octal (`0177.0.0.1`), or hex (`0x7f000001`).
Test shorthand IP formats like `127.1` or IPv6 loopback `[::1]`.

title: PingTool - SSRF CIDR/Hex/Redirect Bypass (Hard)
description: Bypass DNS resolution checks and private CIDR blacklists using HTTP open redirects or DNS rebinding.
hints: Point the health check to an external server you control that issues an HTTP 302 redirect to `http://127.0.0.1/`.
Inspect if the HTTP client follows redirects without re-checking the destination IP against the blacklist.

title: PingTool - Reflected XSS (Easy)
description: Trigger reflected cross-site scripting through the unescaped host parameter displayed in ping output.
hints: Inject `<script>alert(1)</script>` into the target host input.
Check how the ping results page reflects user input directly into the HTML document.

title: PingTool - Reflected XSS Tag Filter Bypass (Medium)
description: Bypass a tag filter that removes `<script>` tags by utilizing event handlers and alternate HTML elements.
hints: Use tags like `` or `
Test case variation or double tags if the filter only strips single occurrences.

title: PingTool - Context-Breaking Reflected XSS (Hard)
description: Break out of JavaScript string literals or attribute contexts when input is reflected inside an existing script block.
hints: Look at where the host parameter is embedded inside `<script>` or attribute quotes.
Escape the string using `"-alert(1)-"` or `</script><script>...` to execute JavaScript.
